title: Reimagining the 1986 C64 game “Mafia” as a modern anime cyberpunk sandbox world. Does this vibe fit the original game?
author: MaximusDunton
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with reimagining the old 1986 Commodore 64 game “Mafia” into a modern stylized cyberpunk anime sandbox world while preserving the original gameplay structure and city layout.

The original game was surprisingly ambitious for its time. It had districts, subway and train travel, casinos, robberies, bribery, gang hiring, and open ended progression. I always loved the sandbox feeling of it because the city itself felt like a living system you could freely interact with.

Instead of going for dark Blade Runner style cyberpunk, I tried a more colorful and readable “playable city” direction inspired by modern anime urban games. The focus was on strong district identity, atmospheric city life, clean visual readability, stylized futuristic urbanism, and a more social open world vibe instead of grimdark noir.

I attached the original C64 images together with several reinterpretations using a consistent visual style system.

I’d honestly love feedback specifically about the vibe and direction. Does this feel like a good modern evolution of the original Mafia atmosphere, or does it drift too far away from the original sandbox feeling?

comments.author: AMadHammer
comments.body: I like the original style more but that is due to seeing anime girls as creepy

replies.author: MaximusDunton
replies.body: That’s fair, and I appreciate the honest feedback. I’m still experimenting with the balance between the retro sandbox vibe and the more stylized futuristic direction.

comments.author: Defiant-Code7676
comments.body: Oh man I really like the idea. Fill it with waifus. You should remake the gameplay then add modern features. I'd totally play it.

replies.author: MaximusDunton
replies.body: Thanks 😄 The sandbox feeling and open city progression of the original game is honestly what interests me most. I’d love to modernize the gameplay systems while keeping that atmosphere and freedom intact.

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: Interesting - I played Crime Fighter a lot back in the day, which was apparently a kind of remake/reimagining/iteration on the idea for DOS.

replies.author: MaximusDunton
replies.body:
Yeah, I discovered Crime Fighter later as well. It definitely had a similar vibe, but what I always loved about the original C64 Mafia was that it was written in BASIC and could be modified so easily.

I ended up removing the built in ending condition and adding joystick control so the game basically turned into an endless sandbox for me. Crime Fighter looked more polished, but it sadly lost a bit of that “the system is yours to change” feeling.
